summary:
SPHEREx Time Machine is an interactive website where users can view and visualize astronomical discoveries accessible to everyone using data directly from NASA’s mission. Our website allows users to enter their coordinates or pick ones on a map and view the stars, comets and galaxies at that time period, which can be picked from our options. By displaying observations in an interactive, video-like viewer, users can easily identify moving objects, changes in brightness, and other astronomical phenomena, including asteroids, comets, stars, and brown dwarfs.
 
Our website’s aim is to transform SPHEREx’s expansive collection of astronomical data captured through out the years of research into one cohesive, engaging website. Through infra-red scans and time-band image comparisons, the tool empowers both astronomy enthusiasts and researchers to investigate the universe, recognize unusual patterns, and contribute to new scientific discoveries. Our goal is to make exploring the changing universe simple,
interactive, and accessible to everyone.
details: SPHEREx Time Machine is a website that allows users to interact and see stars, comets and asteroids by inputting desired coordinates and viewing infra-red images of these astronomical species. The screen of these infra-red photos can be played to view the movement of these asteroids, comets and stars, over 8 periods of time, showing the movement. The main benefit of this website is that users don’t need to browse through thousands of years of data and can view all of this data easily on one singular website. The intended impact is to enable non-professional users to understand and connect to any astronomical interests they may have without having any prior knowledge to space. To develop our project, we have used Base44 via inputting various prompts and adding new prompts to change or alter certain features based off feedback to allow users to have the best possible experience. Our project is creative through adding extra features other than solely viewing the stars and seeing what each object is on the infa-red camera, whilst also describing how each object will be in real-life. Our team considered various factors, such as clear steps defined and bigger fonts to adapt our products to all of our user needs.
